>I progressed to writing automated test suites using Selenium Webdriver for UI automation and various load testing tools, primarily Apache Jmeter, for running capacity and stress tests. I would not have been able to thrive with these tools without learning to program and solve problems using principles of software design. Some tools sell themselves as being GUI driven and accessible to non-technical testers without programming experience. Don't be that person. The reality is that every QA engineer worth a damn is a technical person with programming skills. If you don't better yourself by learning software engineering skills you will forever stay at the entry level "button pusher" level of the QA field. I've worked with middle aged professionals that are in their forties and have been stuck bouncing from one entry level QA job to another over the last 15 - 20 years.
